newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, March 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, March 12.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Wednesday.

- Criminal charges may be brought against key figures in the Hepatitis C scandal following yesterday's decision by the government to send the tribunal of inquiry report to the Director of Public Prosecutions.
- Police have stepped up the hunt for a double killer as chilling new details of the attacks emerged and fears grew that he could strike again.
- Dublin Corporation has salvaged plans for a summer concert by superband U2 in the Phoenix Park.
- Relations between Irish Sugar and its 5,000 beet growers are set to deteriorate following yesterday's company offer of a zero increase in the 1997 raw material price.

- The report of the Hepatitis C tribunal, which the government has referred to the Director of Public Prosecutions, contains startling and severe criticism of named officials of the Blood Transfusion Service Board.
- Permission is being sought from South Dublin County Council for a national freight distribution centre in one of the largest planning applications in the history of the state.
- The housing market is being unduly stimulated by overlending on mortgages by the financial institutions, according to the Irish Auctioneers' and Valuers' Institute.
- The risks for Ireland through delaying membership of EMU to wait for sterling to join could be greater than joining without sterling, according to AIB chief economist John Beggs.
THE EXAMINER - Top former and serving Blood Transfusion Service Board
officers were yesterday held responsible for causing the Hepatitis C scandal.
- Irish punters took a scorching yesterday, not from the blazing sun at Cheltenham but from the bookies who made a killing when none of the home raiders registered a win.
- Police are closing in on a criminal ring behind the multi-million pound theft of computer equipment following the seizure of one million Irish pounds worth of software discs in Limerick yesterday.
- The mother of trawler skipper Daniel O'Driscoll has blamed the owners of Spanish fishing vessel, The Sea Horse, for the collision which led to her son's death.
